heading: INT. SLUMBERLAND MATTRESS OUTLET - WAREHOUSE FLOOR - DAY

units.text: INT. SLUMBERLAND MATTRESS OUTLET - WAREHOUSE FLOOR - DAY
A vast showroom of beds in neat rows under fluorescent light.
Banners scream CLEARANCE and EVERYTHING MUST GO.
A loop of cheerful synth music plays overhead.
Price tags dangle from pillow-top corners.
No customers.
HARLAN PEARCE, 40s, area manager, in a short-sleeved dress shirt with a tie clip, strides down an aisle with a clipboard held like a shield.
He stops at a king-size bed.
He prods the mattress with two fingers.
It sighs.
Three sales. Three. In a week.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: He drags a hand across a stack of throw pillows, scattering them.
He walks to the far end of the row, turns, and walks back.
He picks a pillow off the floor, looks at it, throws it down again.
The front doors hiss.
PAULETTE NWOSU, 30s, a sales associate, her name tag crooked, a tablet clutched to her chest, hurries in with a lanyard around her neck and stops when she sees him.
You're here early.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: I've been here since five.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Doing what?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Counting.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Counting what?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Failures of imagination. This is one.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: He slaps the mattress.
Paulette sets her tablet on a nightstand.
That's a Dreamcloud Elite.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: I know what it is.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Mr. Pearce, are you okay?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: I'm sweating.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: I noticed.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: That's not sweat. That's ambition.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: She glances around the empty aisles.
Far away, the synth music loops back to its first bar.
Regional wants forty percent growth.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: By when?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Friday.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: That's three days.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Yes, Paulette, I know how days work.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: I'm only saying it's not realistic.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Realistic is for people who sell chairs.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: You don't mean that.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: I mean it with my entire heart.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Paulette tilts her head.
She walks to a twin mattress, sits on it, and crosses her legs.
The springs creak.
Can I tell you what I think?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: No.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: I think nobody comes in because the music is depressing.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: The music is upbeat.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: The music is a hostage video.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: The music was chosen by a focus group.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: The focus group needs to sleep.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Harlan stops.
He stares at her.
Something passes over his face: anger, then surprise, then a tiny crack of humor, quickly squashed.
You are on thin ice.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: I'm on a twin.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: He lowers himself onto the king-size bed opposite her.
He sits stiffly at the edge, then, helplessly, lies back.
His shoes stay on the floor.
His tie clip catches the light.
Paulette stays where she is, legs crossed, watching the ceiling with him.
Eight months I've been afraid to say it.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Say what?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: That the music is a hostage video.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: You can say it now.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: It's a hostage video.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Feels better, doesn't it?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: It feels like the beginning of something terrible.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Or something quiet.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: He sits up.
He unclips his tie clip and sets it on the nightstand, as one sets down a gun.
Paulette. Find the remote for the sound system.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: It's in the office.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Get it.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: She hurries off, her footsteps echoing between the beds.
Harlan stays where he is, elbows on his knees, staring at the floor.
In the distance a drawer slides open and slams shut.
Paulette returns at a trot, holding a black remote in both hands.
Here.
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Press the red one.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Are you sure?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: Press it.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: She does.
The synth music cuts out mid-note.
The warehouse is suddenly silent, vast, and peaceful.
They sit on their separate mattresses in the long fluorescent hush.
Neither speaks.
So what do we do now?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: We wait.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: For what?
units.name: PAULETTE

units.text: For someone to come in and be bored.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: She smiles.
He almost does.
Somewhere, a pallet jack rattles past a far loading dock.
The price tags on the pillow-tops stir in the air conditioning, and no one sells anyone anything.
